questions.title: Practice 1 - Count Values Greater Than 50
questions.task: Input 10 integer values. Count how many values are greater than 50. Output the count.
expectedThinking: There are 10 values, so a FOR loop is suitable
A counter is needed to store how many values match
Each value must be checked using IF
The counter increases only when the value is greater than 50

markScheme.criterion: INPUT each value inside the loop

assessment.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE value, count, i : INTEGER

count <- 0

FOR i <- 1 TO 10
    INPUT value

    IF value > 50 THEN
        count <- count + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT count

questions.title: Practice 2 - Array Totals and Counts
questions.task: Input 20 integer values into a 1D array called Numbers. Output the total of all values greater than 50. Also output the number of values less than 20.
expectedThinking: The values must be stored, so an array is needed
Use one loop to input the 20 values
Use a total variable for values greater than 50
Use a count variable for values less than 20
Use IF statements to check each condition
Output both final results after processing

markScheme.criterion: DECLARE index, total and count variables
Correct condition and total for values greater than 50
Correct condition and count for values less than 20

assessment.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE Numbers : ARRAY[1:20] OF INTEGER
DECLARE i, totalGreater, countLess : INTEGER

totalGreater <- 0
countLess <- 0

FOR i <- 1 TO 20
    INPUT Numbers[i]

    IF Numbers[i] > 50 THEN
        totalGreater <- totalGreater + Numbers[i]
    ENDIF

    IF Numbers[i] < 20 THEN
        countLess <- countLess + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT totalGreater
OUTPUT countLess

questions.title: Practice 3 - Past Paper Challenge
questions.question: Q5(a)(i)
questions.task: Paste the exact question text from 9618/22/M/J/21 Q5(a)(i) here. This is the RNum question: declare a 1D array, generate random values from 1 to 200, count values between 66 and 173 inclusive, and output the count.
expectedThinking: Use a loop for 100 array elements
Generate a random number for each element
Store the generated value in the array

markScheme.criterion: Correct random generation in range 1 to 200

assessment.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE RNum : ARRAY[1:100] OF INTEGER
DECLARE i, count : INTEGER

count <- 0

FOR i <- 1 TO 100
    RNum[i] <- RANDOM(1, 200)

    IF RNum[i] >= 66 AND RNum[i] <= 173 THEN
        count <- count + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT count
